evidence: app/ — zero test files, so zero noise
app/src/lib/format.ts — a lean, high-value unit-test target left unexploited
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no low-value tests; scored 3 per the anchor, though a handful of purposeful unit tests would have raised it.

findings.issue: No test infrastructure at all: no runner dependency, no test script, no spec files, despite TanStack officially recommending Vitest + Testing Library and shipping a router/Start test harness.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest + @testing-library/react and a `npm test` script; start with unit tests for format.ts and data.server.ts (mocking fetch), which need no router harness.

findings.issue: Home filtering and pagination (search substring match, type/generation intersection, id<=10000 cut, page clamp, 48-per-page slice) is completely unguarded; an off-by-one shows the wrong cards on every page.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test getHomeData against a stubbed fetch: filter combinations, empty results, page clamping beyond totalPages, boundary at exactly 48/49 matches.

findings.issue: The missing-values-sort-last rule is enforced by special-casing nulls before flipping direction; a refactor that negates the comparator puts em-dash rows first on descending sort, and the acceptance tests only assert present values.
findings.suggestion: Add a table-level test with rows containing null power/accuracy asserting they remain last in both directions.

findings.issue: 404 detection depends on a manually attached `status` property on the fetch error; isNotFound (line 68) silently returns false if that line is lost, converting every not-found page into an unhandled 500.
findings.suggestion: Type the error (a small ApiError class) and unit-test that a 404 from a stubbed fetch yields {notFound:true} while a 500 rethrows.

findings.issue: Promise cache deletes entries only on rejection; if a refactor caches without that cleanup, one transient API failure is cached for the server process's lifetime with no test to catch it.
findings.suggestion: Test that a failed apiGet is retried on the next call and that a success is not refetched.

findings.issue: latestEnglishFlavorText takes the LAST en entry while englishName takes the FIRST; swapping them is a one-line regression affecting every detail page, and whitespace collapse/humanize/dexNumber/height-weight formatting have no assertions.
findings.suggestion: A short table-driven unit test over format.ts: multi-language name lists, flavor entries with \n/\f, mr-mime, id padding, 0.4 m / 6.0 kg.

findings.issue: URL state assembly (omit empty/default params, reset to page 1 on filter change) and validateSearch (lines 14-25) are untested; a regression produces ?q=&page=1 URLs and broken deep links.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test validateSearch and the search-object builder directly, plus a route-level test that changing a select navigates with cleaned params.

findings.issue: Default game selection (highest version-group order), ?game= override validation, method ordering (methodSortKey, line 404) and level-up-then-name sorting are untested; a wrong default shifts every moves table.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test getPokemonPageData with a fixture pokemon record covering game default, invalid game fallback, and table order.

findings.issue: No errorComponent or notFoundComponent on the router; an API 500 surfaces as the framework's default error page with no landmark structure, and nothing exercises that path.
findings.suggestion: Add an error boundary that renders the standard banner/main/footer with a friendly message, and test it by stubbing a 500 from the API.

findings.issue: All server-fn validators are pass-throughs ((data) => data), so no runtime validation guards inputs; a NaN page propagates through the clamp at data.server.ts:308 into matching.slice(NaN, NaN) and an empty list.
findings.suggestion: Use a real validator (zod or manual checks) coercing page to a safe integer, and unit-test the boundary.

summary: The app ships zero tests: no runner, no config, no spec files, and only the acceptance suite as a guard. That's a poor showing given how testable the design is — format.ts is pure and the whole data layer takes fetchable records, so the riskiest logic (filtering, pagination, sorting, 404 detection, URL state) could be covered with plain Vitest in a day. Once the acceptance tests are no longer the only net, refactors of getHomeData, MoveTable's nulls-last sort and apiGet's error handling would very likely break silently.
